name: MonarchResizablePanels
title: ResizablePanels
summary: Two panels with a separator between them that people drag, adjust with TalkBack or move with the arrow keys to share the space.
whenToUse: On a tablet or a large window, for two views people compare or work across: an editor beside its preview, a query above its results. The app keeps the share and restores it.
whenNotToUse: For a list and the detail of the selected item use the Material ListDetailPaneScaffold (see split-layout), which also shows one pane on a phone and has its own drag handle. For a fixed split use a Row with weights.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchResizablePanels(fraction: Float, onFractionChange: (Float) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, axis: MonarchResizablePanelsAxis = MonarchResizablePanelsAxis.Horizontal, range: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Float> = MonarchResizablePanelsDefaults.Range, step: Float = MonarchResizablePanelsDefaults.Step, enabled: Boolean = true, showGrip: Boolean = false, stacksWhenCompact: Boolean = true, handleLabel: String? = null, onResizeFinished: ((Float) -> Unit)? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null, first: @Composable () -> Unit, second: @Composable () -> Unit)
public enum class MonarchResizablePanelsAxis { Horizontal, Vertical }
public object MonarchResizablePanelsDefaults { public val Range: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Float>; public const val Step: Float }

options.name: fraction
options.description: The share of the first panel, from 0 to 1, kept within range. The app owns it; keep it in rememberSaveable or the app's settings to restore the layout.

options.name: onFractionChange
options.description: Called with the new share while the separator moves.

options.name: axis
options.description: Horizontal: side by side, the first panel at the start. Vertical: stacked, the first panel on top; needs a bounded height.

options.name: range
options.description: The smallest and largest share of the first panel, limited to 0..1.

options.name: step
options.description: The share one arrow key press or one TalkBack adjustment moves the separator.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether people can move the separator.

options.name: showGrip
options.description: Draws a grip in the middle of the separator.

options.name: stacksWhenCompact
options.description: On a compact window (narrower than 600dp) side-by-side panels are stacked at their natural height with a divider and no resizing.

options.name: handleLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in name "Resize panels" read by TalkBack.

options.name: onResizeFinished
options.description: Called with the share when a drag ends and after each key press or TalkBack adjustment. Save the layout here.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The interaction source of the separator, for its dragged and focused states.

states.name: resting
states.description: A 1dp line in the default border color in the middle of a 48dp separator.

states.name: dragged or focused
states.description: The line is 2dp and in the accent color; the focus ring surrounds the separator when focused with a keyboard.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The line uses the subtle border color; the separator takes no drag, no key and no adjustment and is announced as disabled.

states.name: stacked
states.description: On a compact window the panels are stacked with a MonarchDivider and there is no separator.

appearance: The line uses the default border color at rest, the accent color while dragged or focused and the subtle border color when disabled; the grip uses the strong border color at rest. The panels draw no surface of their own.
platformNotes: The parity map named a Row with a draggable separator, and ListDetailPaneScaffold where it fits: that scaffold's paneExpansionDragHandle resizes a list and its detail and is documented under split-layout; this component covers any two panels. The web takes any number of panels with alternating handles and sizes in percent; Android, like iOS, takes two panels and one share from 0 to 1, and a third pane is a MonarchResizablePanels nested in a panel. The web keeps the sizes itself (defaultSizes, onLayout); here the app owns the value and onResizeFinished is the moment to save (iOS calls it onResizeEnded; Compose uses "Finished", as in Slider's onValueChangeFinished). Not offered: collapsible panels and a per-handle disabled flag. Stacking on a compact window is the default, as on iOS, because two resizable columns do not fit a phone in portrait. The separator reserves its 48dp touch target between the panels; on iOS the target overlaps the panel edges.
accessibility: The separator is one TalkBack element named "Resize panels" (or handleLabel).
Its state description is the share of the first panel as a whole percentage in the device locale, for example "40%".
It has slider semantics (a progress range with a set-progress action), so TalkBack's adjust gestures move it by step and the value is limited to range.

With a hardware keyboard the separator takes focus and draws the focus ring. The arrow keys along the axis move it by step in the direction they point, so left and right swap in a right-to-left layout; Home and End move it to the ends of range.
Its touch target is 48dp across, reserved in the layout between the panels.
In a right-to-left layout the first panel is on the right and dragging follows the finger.
The active state is a thicker line as well as the accent color.
The panels are not animated while they resize, so there is nothing for reduced motion to turn off.
edgeCases: A fraction outside range is shown at the nearest end of range; a range outside 0..1 is limited to it.
A vertical layout without a bounded height gives each panel its natural height and the share has no effect.
A panel with content wider than its share is clipped by its own content's layout, not by this component; make panel content scroll or wrap.

parityExceptions.reason: NATIVE GAP: The web left panel is collapsible (drag it below its minimum to collapse) and the second panel has a 30 percent minimum; native has one range for the divider and no collapse.
